reasoning:
All three claims in the finding are verified against the source:

1. Dependency range mismatch: pyproject.toml line 12 declares 'duckdb>=1.3.2,<1.6', permitting 1.4.x and 1.5.x.

2. Validated only on 1.3.2: pybridge.py lines 31-34 states explicitly 'Validated on duckdb 1.3.2 / Linux x86-64 / libstdc++. The pybind11 instance layout and the DuckDBPyConnection struct layout are implementation details... Re-verify offsets when upgrading duckdb.'

3. No runtime guard: pybridge.py has no version check anywhere. grep over all of numbduck/pybridge.py, numbduck/utils.py, and numbduck/ducklib.py found no duckdb version assertion or skip gate guarding these offsets.

The +16 pybind11 instance offset (line 59) and +32 DuckDBPyConnection member offset (line 62) are read unconditionally regardless of the installed duckdb version. The SELECT 1 validation (lines 65-72) is a best-effort guard that will typically segfault rather than raise RuntimeError when the offset is wrong (as analyzed in sibling finding PBR-COR-2), so it does not close the gap.

The reviewer's characterization is accurate: a mismatch between the declared supported range (<1.6) and the actually validated ABI (1.3.2 only) exists, with no runtime safeguard. The severity 'medium' is appropriate — the impact if the layout changed between 1.3.2 and a later minor would be memory corruption, but the confidence is medium because we cannot confirm from code alone that the DuckDBPyConnection struct layout actually changed in 1.4.x or 1.5.x. The finding is not overblown; the code's own docstring confirms the limitation.
